scenes.title: The Magic Seed
narration: Have you ever wondered how a tiny mango seed becomes a big tree?
It all starts when we bury a seed in the warm garden soil.
The seed waits patiently for a little bit of water and sunshine.

scenes.title: Sprouting and Growing
narration: Soon, a tiny root pushes down to drink water from the earth.
Then, a little green shoot pokes up through the soil to find light.
The plant grows leaves to catch sunlight and make its own food.

scenes.title: From Flower to Fruit
narration: Look, our little plant is now big enough to grow a beautiful flower.
Bees visit the flower to help it turn into a yummy fruit.
Inside that juicy mango, there are new seeds waiting to start again.

scenes.title: Nature's Amazing Cycle
narration: Plants grow from seeds, make flowers, and create new seeds for the future.
Every plant follows this special journey to help our world stay green.
Think about it, what do you think would happen if plants never made seeds?

scenes.title: A Pond Discovery
narration: Have you ever seen tiny jelly bubbles in a pond near your house?
These are frog eggs, the start of an incredible journey.
How do these tiny dots turn into jumping green frogs?

scenes.title: Growing Up Underwater
narration: First, the egg hatches into a little tadpole that swims like a fish.
Tadpoles use special gills to breathe underwater while they eat pond plants.
Slowly, the tadpole starts to grow two back legs.
Soon, front legs pop out and its long tail gets shorter.

scenes.title: Becoming A Frog
narration: Now, the little froglet climbs onto a lily pad to breathe air.
Its tail disappears completely as it prepares to hop on land.
Finally, it becomes an adult frog ready to catch flies.

scenes.title: Lifecycle Recap
narration: So, the cycle goes from egg, to tadpole, to froglet, and finally, adult.
Every stage is important for the frog to grow strong.
Think about it: why do you think frogs need water to lay their eggs?

scenes.title: Spotting Animals at the Park
narration: Have you seen a barking dog and a flying pigeon at the park?
Why are some animals fuzzy and others have shiny feathers?
Today, we will learn how scientists group these amazing creatures.

scenes.title: Vertebrates and Invertebrates
narration: Some animals have a strong backbone inside their bodies called a spine.
These are called vertebrates, like you, me, and the tiger.
Others have no bones at all, like a wiggly earthworm.

scenes.title: Examples of Animal Groups
narration: Mammals like a cow drink milk and have warm bodies.
Birds have feathers and lay eggs in a cozy nest.
Fish live in water and use gills to breathe easily.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: We group animals by their bodies, like having a backbone.
Think about it: is a butterfly a vertebrate or invertebrate?

scenes.title: The Animal Home Hunt
narration: Look at the squirrel in the park, where does it sleep at night?
Every animal needs a special place called a habitat to survive.
A habitat gives them food, water, and a safe place to rest.

scenes.title: Different Homes for Different Friends
narration: Some animals like the desert, where it is very hot and dry.
Others prefer the deep blue ocean, where they swim all day long.
High up in the cool Himalayan mountains, the snow leopard stays warm.
Each habitat has special features that help specific animals live there.

scenes.title: Example: The Mango Orchard
narration: Think about a mango orchard in India full of sweet fruit.
Parrots find plenty of mangoes to eat right in the trees.
The thick leaves keep the birds safe from the hot sun.
If we took the parrot to the desert, it would struggle to find food.

scenes.title: Bringing It All Together
narration: Remember, a habitat provides everything an animal needs to grow.
From the hot desert to the cool forest, every spot is home.
Think about it: what would happen to a fish if its pond dried up?

scenes.title: The Curious Animal Parade
narration: Have you ever wondered why a camel has a hump but a fish has fins?
Meet Rohan at the zoo looking at the tall giraffe eating leaves.
Why is the giraffe built that way and not like a little mouse?

scenes.title: What Are Adaptations?
narration: Adaptations are special body parts or behaviors that help animals live in their homes.
Just like you wear a raincoat in the monsoon, animals have gear for their climate.
These features help them find food, stay safe, and keep their temperature just right.

scenes.title: The Camel in the Desert
narration: Think of a camel living in the hot Thar Desert near Rajasthan.
Its wide, flat feet help it walk on soft sand without sinking.
That big hump stores fat, giving the camel energy when food is hard to find.
Its long eyelashes keep out the blowing sand so it can see clearly.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Animals adapt to their environment to survive and thrive in the wild.
Every feature, from a beak to a fur coat, has a special job to do.
Think about it: what special body part would you want if you lived underwater?

scenes.title: A Hungry Garden
narration: Have you ever wondered what the little birds in your park eat for breakfast?
Everything living needs energy to grow, run, and play all day long.
Let's discover how energy moves from the sun to your garden visitors.

scenes.title: The Food Chain Steps
narration: It all starts with plants, which use sunlight to make their own food.
Next, a hungry grasshopper eats the plant to get that stored energy.
Then, a lizard catches the grasshopper to fuel its own quick movements.
This special path of who eats whom is called a food chain.

scenes.title: An Indian Garden Example
narration: Imagine a bright green neem tree in a Delhi park.
A caterpillar nibbles on the neem leaves to get strong.
A small sparrow swoops down and eats the caterpillar for a snack.

scenes.title: Wrap Up
narration: Plants make energy, and animals pass that energy along the chain.
Without this chain, animals would not have the fuel they need to survive.
Think about it: what would happen to the chain if all the plants disappeared?

scenes.title: Why Do We Eat?
narration: Have you ever wondered why Rohan feels so tired after playing cricket?
Our bodies are like cars that need special fuel to run.
That fuel comes from the yummy food we eat every day.

scenes.title: The Food Groups
narration: First, carbohydrates give us quick energy to run and jump.
Next, proteins help our muscles grow big and strong.
Finally, vitamins in fruits protect us from getting sick.

scenes.title: A Healthy Plate
narration: Let's build Priya's lunch plate with a mix of these.
Add a scoop of dal for protein and rice for energy.
Don't forget crunchy carrots to keep your eyes bright.

scenes.title: Stay Strong Everyday
narration: Remember, eat a rainbow of colors to stay healthy.
Avoid too many sugary snacks that make you crash.
What is your favorite healthy vegetable to eat for dinner?

scenes.title: Everyday Shapes and Flows
narration: Arav is thirsty after school, so he pours some cold water into his favorite glass.
He holds a hard ice cube in his hand, but it does not change its shape.
Why can we hold ice, but water spills everywhere? Let's explore the states of matter.

scenes.title: Understanding Tiny Particles
narration: In solids like a wooden block, tiny particles are packed tightly together and stay still.
In liquids like milk, the particles are looser and can slide past each other easily.
In gases like the steam from hot tea, the particles zip around fast and fill everything.

scenes.title: Watching Matter Change
narration: Imagine an ice cube from your freezer starts to melt on a warm sunny day.
As it gets warmer, the solid ice turns into a liquid puddle of water.
If you boil that water, it turns into invisible steam, which is a gas.

scenes.title: Quick Recap and Challenge
narration: Matter can be a solid, a liquid, or a gas depending on how particles move.
Heating or cooling things can make them change from one state to another.
Think about it: Is the air inside a balloon a solid, a liquid, or a gas?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Motion
narration: Have you ever wondered why your football rolls across the school field?
It does not move by itself, it needs a push.
This push or pull is what scientists call a force.

scenes.title: Pushing and Pulling Objects
narration: When you push a heavy bag of apples, you apply force.
When you pull open a drawer to find your pen, that is force too.
Forces can make things start moving or stop moving.

scenes.title: Helping Rohan at Home
narration: Rohan wants to move his toy box across the room.
He pushes the box forward with his hands.
The box slides faster as he pushes harder.
When he stops pushing, the box slows down and stops.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: A force is simply a push or a pull.
Forces change how objects move, speed up, or stop.
Think about it, what other things in your house do you push or pull?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Shadows
narration: Have you ever noticed your shadow following you while walking to school?
A shadow is a dark shape made when something blocks the light.
Why does a shadow only appear when it is sunny or bright?

scenes.title: How Shadows Work
narration: Light travels in a straight line until it hits an object.
If the object is opaque, light cannot pass through it.
The light goes around the object, but the space behind stays dark.
That dark space is the shadow we see on the ground.

scenes.title: Rohan and the Torch
narration: Rohan holds a toy elephant in front of a bright torch.
The elephant blocks the light beam perfectly.
A clear elephant shadow appears on the white wall.
When Rohan moves the torch closer, the shadow gets bigger.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Remember, light travels straight and objects block it to make shadows.
Shadows change size depending on where the light source is.
Think about it: why do your shadows look longer at sunset than at noon?

scenes.title: The Body's Framework
narration: Have you ever wondered how Rohan runs so fast on the playground?
It is because your body has a strong skeleton inside.
Your bones act like a hard frame to hold you up.

scenes.title: Bones and Muscles Teamwork
narration: Bones are strong, but they cannot move on their own.
Muscles are stretchy tissues that attach to your bones.
When muscles pull on the bone, your arm or leg moves.

scenes.title: A Bicep at Work
narration: Let us look at your arm when you lift a heavy school bag.
Your bicep muscle gets shorter and tighter to lift your forearm.
Then, the muscle relaxes to let your arm go back down.

scenes.title: Keep Moving Strong
narration: Bones provide the shape, and muscles provide the movement.
Eat healthy food and play outside to keep them strong.
Think about it, what would happen if you had no bones at all?

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you ever wondered where your yummy lunch goes after you swallow it?
It travels inside your body to become the energy you need for playing.
This process is called digestion, and it happens like a big slide inside you.

scenes.title: The Steps of Digestion
narration: First, your teeth chew the food into tiny, soft pieces.
Next, it travels down a long tube into your tummy, the stomach.
Inside the stomach, juices mix with food to turn it into a thick soup.
Then, it moves to the intestines to soak up all the good nutrients.

scenes.title: A Real Life Example
narration: Imagine eating a crisp apple for your school snack.
Your teeth crunch the apple so it is easy to swallow.
The stomach squeezes the apple bits until they become a smooth liquid.
Finally, your body takes the energy from that apple to help you run.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Chewing starts it, the stomach mashes it, and intestines take the nutrients.
Your body works hard every single day to turn food into you.
Think about it: Why is it important to chew your food slowly?

scenes.title: The Crunchy Apple Mystery
narration: Aarav is eating a crunchy apple in the school playground.
Have you ever wondered why we have different shapes of teeth?
Our teeth are like tools that help us eat our favorite snacks.

scenes.title: Meet Your Tooth Team
narration: In the front, we have sharp incisors for biting into food.
Next to them are pointy canines that help tear tougher bites.
At the back, flat molars grind food until it is soft.

scenes.title: A Day With Your Teeth
narration: Think of a crunchy carrot from the market.
First, your incisors take a big bite out of the carrot.
Then, your back molars crush it into small, safe pieces to swallow.

scenes.title: Keep Them Sparkling
narration: Remember to brush twice a day to keep your tooth tools strong.
Healthy teeth help us talk clearly and eat yummy meals.
Think about it: What would happen if we only had one type of tooth shape?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Sound
narration: Have you ever wondered how your friend's voice reaches your ears from across the playground?
When Rohan claps his hands, he creates a tiny movement in the air.
These movements are called vibrations, and they are invisible to our eyes.

scenes.title: How Sound Moves
narration: Think of vibrations like ripples moving across a pond after dropping a stone.
Sound waves push the air particles forward, one after another, in a long chain.
The sound travels through the air until it finally reaches your ear.

scenes.title: Example: Playing the Tabla
narration: When Priya plays the tabla, the skin on top starts shaking really fast.
This shaking pushes the air, creating waves that travel across the room.
When the waves hit your ear, you hear the lovely music playing.

scenes.title: Summary and Questions
narration: Sound starts with vibrations and travels through the air like waves.
Without these vibrations, we would not be able to hear anything at all.
Think about it: Can sound travel in a place where there is no air?

scenes.title: The Day and Night Mystery
narration: Have you noticed the bright sun wakes us up and the moon glows at night?
Why does the sky change colors like magic while we play in the park?
Let us find out why these two friends take turns in the sky.

scenes.title: How the Earth Spins
narration: The Earth is like a giant spinning top that never stops moving.
As India faces the sun, it is bright daytime for us.
When we spin away from the sun, it gets dark and nighttime begins.
The sun stays still, but our spinning makes it look like it moves.

scenes.title: The Moon's Cool Tricks
narration: The moon does not make its own light like a glowing bulb.
It acts like a mirror, bouncing the sun's light back to our eyes.
Sometimes we see a full moon, and other times just a thin slice.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: The sun is a star, and the moon is our rocky neighbor.
Day and night happen because the Earth keeps spinning around.
Think about it: if the Earth stopped spinning, what would happen to our days?

scenes.title: The Curious Morning Sky
narration: Ananya looks out her window at the fluffy white clouds in Delhi.
Have you ever wondered where rain comes from before it hits the ground?
Let us go on a journey to find out how clouds turn into rain.

scenes.title: How Clouds Are Made
narration: The hot sun warms up water in rivers and lakes.
This warm water turns into invisible mist called water vapor.
High in the sky, the vapor cools down to form tiny cloud droplets.
When millions of these droplets join together, they create a big, heavy cloud.

scenes.title: The Rain Falls Down
narration: Inside the cloud, droplets bump into each other and grow bigger.
Soon, the cloud gets too heavy to hold all that water.
Gravity pulls the drops, and they fall down as refreshing rain.
The water lands in the park, helping the flowers grow tall.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Sun warms water, vapor rises, and clouds eventually release rain.
Everything happens in a cycle that repeats every single time it rains.
Think about it: What would happen to our thirsty plants if it never rained?

scenes.title: Where We Live
narration: Have you ever wondered why we do not fall off the Earth?
We live on a giant ball spinning in space called Earth.
Everything we see is held down by a secret force called gravity.

scenes.title: What Makes Earth Special
narration: Most of our Earth is covered in beautiful blue water.
We have rocky ground, tall mountains, and green forests.
A thin layer of air called the atmosphere wraps us like a blanket.

scenes.title: A Trip Around India
narration: Imagine flying over the snowy Himalayan mountains in the north.
Then, we glide down to the green plains where farmers grow wheat.
Finally, we visit the sunny beaches by the vast Indian Ocean.

scenes.title: Keeping Earth Happy
narration: Earth gives us water, air, and food to grow strong.
We must take care of our planet by keeping it clean.
Think about it: what is one way you can help Earth today?

scenes.title: The Warm Morning Tea
narration: Have you ever touched a hot cup of chai and felt your fingers get warm?
Why does the heat move from the cup into your hands?
Let us discover how heat travels in our daily lives.

scenes.title: Learning About Heat
narration: Heat is a special kind of energy that makes things feel warm.
It always likes to travel from a warmer place to a cooler place.
This movement happens until everything is the same temperature.

scenes.title: Cooking Breakfast at Home
narration: Imagine your mother frying a crispy dosa on a hot metal pan.
The stove gives heat to the metal pan, making it very hot.
Then, the hot pan gives its heat to the cool dosa batter.
Soon, the dosa is cooked perfectly and ready to eat.

scenes.title: Quick Heat Summary
narration: Heat is energy that moves from hot things to cold things.
It keeps our food warm and our homes cozy.
Think about it: Why does an ice cream melt when you hold it?

scenes.title: Where does rain go?
narration: Have you ever wondered where rain goes after it splashes on the ground in your garden?
Does it just disappear, or does it go on a secret adventure?
Today, let us follow a tiny drop of water on its big trip around Earth.

scenes.title: How Water Moves Up
narration: When the hot sun shines on a pond, the water gets warm and turns into invisible vapor.
This process is called evaporation, and it lifts the water high up into the blue sky.
High up in the cool air, the vapor turns back into tiny water droplets to form clouds.

scenes.title: Rain Falls Down Again
narration: Imagine a big, fluffy cloud over a farm in Punjab getting heavy with too much water.
When the cloud cannot hold the water anymore, it falls down as cool, refreshing rain.
The water flows into rivers and fills up our buckets, ready to start all over again.

scenes.title: The Never Ending Loop
narration: Water goes from the ground to the sky and back down in a never ending loop.
We call this repeating journey the water cycle, and it keeps our planet green and healthy.
Think about it: how would your day change if the rain decided to take a long holiday?

scenes.title: The World Around Us
narration: Look around your home or park, what do you see that comes from nature?
Everything we use starts as a natural resource, like the sun, air, or water.
Have you ever wondered where the wood for your pencil or water comes from?

scenes.title: What are Natural Resources?
narration: Natural resources are things found in nature that humans use to survive.
Some resources like sunlight and wind never run out, so we call them renewable.
Others like coal or oil take millions of years to form, so we must save them.

scenes.title: A Day in India
narration: Think of a farmer in Punjab using water from the river to grow wheat.
Or sunlight hitting solar panels on a rooftop in Delhi to make electricity.
Even the iron used to build our trains comes from rocks dug from the ground.

scenes.title: Protecting Our Earth
narration: Nature gives us so much, so we must use these gifts carefully every day.
By saving water and turning off lights, we help our planet stay healthy.
Think about it: which natural resource could you use a little less of today?
